title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-20
lineage: SBD > MR > 7inch Reel (2nd Gen) > Revox A-77 Alesis Masterlink ML-9600 (24/96) > CDR (16/44.1) > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A classic late‑’70 acoustic‑electric set with a monster Not Fade Away and superb Easy Wind, but persistent tape hiss and occasional clipping keep the soundboard recording only fair.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – the acoustic set (Uncle John’s Band, Lay Me Down, Ripple, Rosalie McFall, Truckin’, Big Railroad Blues) shines, and the second‑set jams like Not Fade Away, Caution/Feedback and Easy Wind are described as electrifying.  The source is an SBD with noticeable hiss, level swings and distortion on the Caution track, so while the music is top‑tier, the audio fidelity ranges from good to fair.

ai_rating.rationale: Average user rating ≈4.1 stars; reviewers overwhelmingly praise the show (70% weight) while noting moderate‑to‑poor recording issues (30% weight), yielding a combined score around 4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable tape hiss and occasional clipping, especially on the Caution jam; level fluctuations give parts of the mix a distorted feel, but overall listenable for a 1970 SBD.

standout_songs: Acoustic set (Uncle John's Band, Lay Me Down, Ripple, Rosalie McFall, Truckin', Big Railroad Blues)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A strong acoustic first half followed by a high‑energy electric second set; the transitions into long jams keep the momentum and showcase the band’s 1970 peak.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar described as crisp and solid despite the hiss, with his playing anchoring both sets.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s solo on Easy Wind highlighted as a standout moment.
band_member_comments.Keys: Guest mandolin (Grisman/David Nelson) praised for adding beauty to the acoustic set; occasional piano/organ noted but not detailed.
